title: Numerical Methods
seo_title: Year 13 A Level Maths: Numerical Methods Worksheets
standard_text: Locate roots of f(x) = 0 by considering changes of sign; solve equations approximately using iterative methods and the Newton–Raphson method; understand and use numerical integration of functions, including the trapezium rule.
meta_desc: Free Year 13 A level maths worksheets on numerical methods: change of sign, iteration, the Newton–Raphson method and the trapezium rule. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A change of sign shows a root (if f is continuous).
body_html:
How it works

If f is continuous and f(a), f(b) have different signs, there is a root between a and b. Iteration: xn+1 = g(xn). Newton–Raphson: xn+1 = xn − f(xn)/f′(xn).

Trapezium rule: ∫ y dx ≈ ½h[y0 + yn + 2(y1 + … + yn−1)].

Example

Trapezium rule, h = 1, y = 1, 4, 9

½ × 1 × (1 + 9 + 2 × 4)

Answer: 9

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to double the middle y-values.
  • Using the wrong sign in Newton–Raphson.
  • Rounding too early in an iteration.

faq.q: What does the Newton–Raphson method do?
faq.a: It uses the tangent at xₙ to find a better estimate of the root: xₙ₊₁ = xₙ − f(xₙ)/f′(xₙ).

faq.q: Is the trapezium rule an overestimate?
faq.a: For a curve that bends upwards (convex) it overestimates; for one that bends downwards it underestimates.
